items.title: Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dead at 65, Band Shares Loving Tributes
items.summary:
Duran Duran has announced the death of its iconic guitarist Andy Taylor “following a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer.” He was 65.

“Andy passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by family, on Monday 23rd November,” the “Hungry Like the Wolf” band announced in a Wednesday, November 25, statement .

Andy became one of the classic “Fab Five” members of Duran Duran when he joined the New Wave band in 1980, along with singer Simon Le Bon , keyboardist Nick Rhodes , drummer Roger Taylor and bassist John Taylor . (Andy, Roger, 66, and John, 66, were not related.)

The group went on to sell more than 100 million records worldwide and received a coveted star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1993. They were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022. (Andy left Duran Duran originally in 1986 but later returned for a five-year reunion stint between 2001 to 2006.)

The Most Shocking Celebrity Deaths of All Time: Hayden Panettiere and More 

Andy was also part of the 1980s supergroup the Power Station, along with Duran Duran bandmate John, Chic drummer Tony Thompson and frontman Robert Palme r. Formed in 1984, the Power Station scored U.S. Top 10 hits with “Some Like It Hot” and a cover for T. Rex’s “Get It On.”

Le Bon, 68, announced during Duran Duran’s Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony in 2022 that Andy was unable to attend after being diagnosed with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.

“Andy was there at the very beginning of our story,” Duran Duran said on Wednesday. “From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and…
items.t: Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dead at 65, Band Shares Loving Tributes

items.title: Aaron Rodgers' Most Controversial Moments On and Off the Football Field
items.summary:
Aaron Rodgers is one of the best-ever quarterbacks to play in the NFL, but it’s often his antics off the field that get the most people talking.

Rodgers — who was the Green Bay Packers superstar quarterback for 18 seasons before joining the New York Jets in 2023 and the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2025 — came under fire in November 2021 when it was revealed he misled people about his COVID-19 vaccination status when he told reporters that he was “immunized” when he hadn’t actually been vaccinated.

The athlete defended his use of the phrase, calling it “the truth.”

“Had there been a follow-up to my statement that I’d been immunized, I would have responded with this: I would have said, ‘Look, I’m not some sort of anti-vax-flat-Earther. I’m somebody who’s a critical thinker,’” Rodgers later explained on the Pat McAfee Show . “I march to the beat of my own drum. I believe strongly in bodily autonomy, [in the] ability to make choices for your body, not to have to acquiesce to some woke culture or crazed group of individuals who say you have to do something.”

He raised eyebrows again in November 2026, when his controversial comments about Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy amid his benching ended with the team releasing the quarterback hours later.

McCarthy, who previously coached Rodgers during the quarterback’s time at the Green Bay Packers, explained, “We got to a point, we’d talked about some things, communication, things like that, and there was an ultimatum made [that was] clearly out of his job description. So it was my decision to bench him.”

items.title: 'Hunting Wives' Author May Cobb Addresses Show's Changes Before Season 2
items.summary:
The Hunting Wives author May Cobb is addressing the show’s deviation from the book ahead of the highly-anticipated season 2.

“I feel like [creator] Rebecca [Cutter] did such a great job of keeping the spirit of the book — the unhinged spirit — very much intact,” Cobb exclusively told Us . “The first scene that I got to see them film was the skeet shooting scene — and that scene to me in the book was near and dear to my heart. So I was so happy that it stayed and it was the first one I got to see.”

Cobb called it an “ out of body experience ” watching her scenes come to life, adding, “So that was really really cool because that was Sophie’s initiation into this world. That’s the moment where she’s going to cross over and decide to descend with the hunting wives.”

Based on Cobb’s book of the same name, The Hunting Wives introduced Sophie ( Brittany Snow ), who moved from Boston to an East Texas town where she found herself drawn to prominent socialite Margo ( Malin Åkerman ). While some became invested in the murder at the center of the series, The Hunting Wives also provided plenty of entertainment with guns, drinking and steamy onscreen hookups.

What 'The Hunting Wives' Cast Has Said About the Book Changes in the Show 

“Rebecca told me when we first met that she was going to change up the ending to where Margo lives. My response to her was, ‘Where were you when I was writing this book? items.title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Reach Settlement in Years-Long Winery Battle
items.summary:
Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a years-long legal dispute over the sale of their French winery, Château Miraval.

“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” representatives of Jolie, 51, and Pitt, 62, said in a Wednesday, November 25, statement to Us . “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”

The couple first gained a controlling interest in the 1,200-acre winery in the South of France in 2008.

They began selling their own rosé in March 2013, before saying “I do” at the chateau in August 2014. Things got sour, however, after Jolie and Pitt filed for divorce in 2016.

Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie's Winery Battle Settled: Everything to Know 

According to a February 2022 lawsuit, Pitt alleged that Jolie illegally sold her shares of Miraval to Tenute del Mondo, the wine division of the Stoli group owned by Russian businessman Yuri Shefler .

Pitt claimed that both parties agreed not to sell their Miraval shares without the other’s permission. In his filing, Pitt argued that his ex-wife made the business decision without his knowledge or explicit consent.

“Through the purported sale, Jolie sought to inflict harm on Pitt,” the lawsuit alleged. “Jolie knew and intended that Shefler and his affiliates would try to control the business Pitt had built and to undermine Pitt’s investment in Miraval.”

Us has learned the litigation between Pitt and Stoli will continue despite the recent settlement involving Jolie.

items.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade 2026 Postponed for the 1st Time in History
items.summary:
For the first time in history, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be held after Thanksgiving.

Multiple outlets reported on Wednesday, November 25, that the 2026 parade — which marks the tradition’s 100th anniversary — has been postponed to Saturday, November 28, due to forecasted severe weather.

“With severe weather expected on Thanksgiving Day, and out of an abundance of caution, in partnership with the City, the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed,” Macy’s said in a Wednesday statement.

The parade is expected to begin on Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET.

“Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday, and we will share additional details as they are finalized,” the statement continued. “We are incredibly grateful to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who make this extraordinary tradition possible. We can’t wait to celebrate 100 years of Parade magic together on Saturday.”

A powerful coastal storm with strong winds is set to hit the New York City area on Thursday, November 26, leading to safety concerns. It was previously reported that the parade’s famous balloons were at risk of being grounded on Thursday due to the forecasted weather. (The last time balloons were grounded occurred in 1971. In 2006 and 2019, balloons were flown at a lower height due to the wind.)

items.t: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade 2026 Postponed for the 1st Time in History

items.title: Boy, 9, Critically Injured After Falling Out of SUV Driven by His Drunk Uncle
items.summary:
A 9-year-old boy in Texas was critically injured after he fell out of a moving SUV that was driven by his uncle who was under the influence.

The boy’s uncle, Oscar Pereira Bustill , was arrested on Sunday, November 22, and has been charged with one count of driving while intoxicated for the second time in less than three years. He was previously hit with a DWI charge in 2023, which prosecutors later dismissed after Bustill, 32, agreed to enter a court-ordered pretrial intervention program.

Authorities learned of the incident in the early hours of Sunday when police responded to the intersection of Bellaire Boulevard and Boone Road in Houston, Texas, around 3:00 a.m. after they received a report of an injured child, according to KHOU .

Officers with the Houston Police Department and emergency medical personnel responded to the scene, and the child was rushed to Memorial Hermann Hospital for treatment.

Police spoke with the other passengers in the vehicle, who explained that Bustill was driving the vehicle with the 9-year-old boy, two other children and three adults inside, per the Houston Chronicle .

One of the passengers said that the group had been at a family member’s quinceañera earlier in the night, according to KTRK . She told authorities she believed Bustill had about four drinks during the party.

That witness also said that she had initially been driving the car, but Bustill took over because she was feeling sick.
